original_query: select      cd_gender,     cd_marital_status,     cd_education_status,     hd_vehicle_count,     count(*) as cnt from     store_sales,     web_sales,     date_dim d1,     date_dim d2,     customer,     inventory,     store,     warehouse,     item,     customer_demographics,     household_demographics,     customer_address     where       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk       and ws_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk       and ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk 			and d2.d_date between d1.d_date and (d1.d_date + interval '30' day)       and ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk       and inv_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and inv_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk       and inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss_quantity       and s_state = w_state       AND i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')       and i_manager_id IN (3, 15, 17, 26, 43, 44, 55, 70, 82, 95)       and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk       and c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk       and c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk       and ca_state in ('IN', 'LA', 'NE', 'NM', 'OH')       and d1.d_year = 2001       and ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100     group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, hd_vehicle_count     order by cnt     ;
rewritten_query:
WITH store_state AS (
    SELECT s_state, COUNT(*)::bigint AS store_cnt
    FROM store
    GROUP BY s_state
),
filtered_item AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
      AND i_manager_id IN (3, 15, 17, 26, 43, 44, 55, 70, 82, 95)
),
filtered_customer AS (
    SELECT c.c_customer_sk,
           c.c_current_cdemo_sk,
           c.c_current_hdemo_sk
    FROM customer c
    JOIN customer_address ca
      ON ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
    WHERE ca.ca_state IN ('IN', 'LA', 'NE', 'NM', 'OH')
)
SELECT
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    hd.hd_vehicle_count,
    SUM(st.store_cnt)::bigint AS cnt
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON d1.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND d1.d_year = 2001
 AND d1.d_date >= DATE '2001-01-01'
 AND d1.d_date <  DATE '2002-01-01'
JOIN filtered_item i
  ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
JOIN filtered_customer c
  ON c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
JOIN web_sales ws
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON d2.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN d1.d_date AND d1.d_date + INTERVAL '30' day
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN DATE '2001-01-01' AND DATE '2002-01-30'
JOIN warehouse w
  ON w.w_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
JOIN store_state st
  ON st.s_state = w.w_state
JOIN inventory inv
  ON inv.inv_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND inv.inv_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND inv.inv_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
 AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss.ss_quantity
JOIN customer_demographics cd
  ON cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON hd.hd_demo_sk = c.c_current_hdemo_sk
GROUP BY
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    hd.hd_vehicle_count
ORDER BY cnt;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The original join 'store' only matches on s_state = w_state, multiplying every result row by the number of stores in that state. Since store columns are not used in output or grouping, replace the join with a pre-aggregated store count per state and use SUM(store_cnt), preserving the exact row multiplicities of COUNT(*).

Early-filter customers by ca_state through a CTE joining customer and customer_address, so the fact tables only join against the reduced customer set. Similarly pre-filter items by category and manager_id.

Add implied date bounds: d1.d_date within 2001 and d2.d_date within [2001-01-01, 2002-01-30], which are logically implied by d1.d_year = 2001 and the 30-day window. These extra sargable predicates help prune date_dim and can improve index usage.
Convert implicit comma joins into explicit ANSI JOINs, making join order and semantics clearer and enabling the optimizer to propagate filtered dimension keys (item/customer) before fact joins.
